description:
First rendering work: display the git history of a v0.1-shape conversation repo as a tree view. Per ARCH §7.1.

=== What to build ===

- Pure-Rust view-model module: 'GitTree::from_repo(repo_root: &Path) -> Result<GitTree, Error>'. Reads the git history (via git2 or libgit2), produces a view-model describing commits, parents, branches, refs. Pure function of FS state at the current ref.
- Dioxus component that renders GitTree as a visual tree view. Thin — all logic is in the view-model.
- For v0.1-shape repos: the 'tree' is a linear sequence of commits on main, each with an exchanges/<ts>-<short-id>.json. Render each commit with its timestamp + exchange id + a truncated user-message preview read from the JSON.
- As v0.2/v0.3/v0.4 land, the renderer naturally extends to show branches, sub-branches, merges. This task does NOT attempt to pre-implement those — it only handles the flat v0.1 shape, in a way that won't require rewriting when branches arrive.

=== Out of scope ===

- Live updates — that's wired via the filesystem watcher in a later task.
- Navigation / click-to-focus — v0.5 epic success criterion but deferred to a follow-up.
- Streaming-text indicators — same.

=== Dependencies ===

- Blocks on 'UI skeleton' (binary to hang the component off).
- Soft-blocks on 'UI: filesystem watcher module' for live updates, but the initial version can render once at startup; live wiring is a later task.

=== Testing ===

- Fixture repos under 'tests/fixtures/v01/' — small, hand-constructed real lernie repos (not mocks) with known commit shapes. Test via 'GitTree::from_repo(fixture_path)' returning the expected view-model.
- Dioxus render test: construct a GitTree with a known shape, render via VirtualDom, assert the output contains the expected text.
- 100% line coverage on view-model functions.
title: UI: git-tree renderer for v0.1-shape repos
